newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates steady, liquidity better.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates steady, liquidity better.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were steady on Wednesday despite improved liquidity, dealers said.
"The banks' accounts have been replenished. Some 54 million kuna is still left on the supply side," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.

Call money loans, granted at a regular 10.5 percent, accounted for more than half of the morning's 27.5 million kuna trade. Banks also had 64.9 million kuna in outstanding central bank Lombard loans which are granted at 9.5 percent for 12 working days each month.
Eight-day loans were granted at 12 percent, one-month funds at 15 and 16 percent and two-month deals were struck at 17, 18 and 19 percent.
Some seven million kuna worth of two-month loans was still sought by banks, but all the long-term funds were exhausted.
There was no overnight trade on Tuesday and the banks' accounts totalled 486 million kuna. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075
